title: Batch extraction of morphological and color metrics from invertebrate samples.
author: Michael D Weiser
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.byt4pwqw

steps.title: Create Camera Profile for Color Checking
steps.instruction: Perform this one-time setup to ensure color accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Take a full resolution image of the X-Rite ColorChecker Mini Classic.
Open the .CR2 raw image in Adobe Photoshop, ensuring the ColorChecker is fully in frame (do not open as .tif).
Save the image as a .DNG (Digital Negative) file.
Open the .DNG file in the ColorChecker Passport application.
Allow the application to detect the ColorChecker and click 'Create Profile'.
Save the camera profile and quit the application.

steps.title: Set Up Camera System
steps.instruction: Configure the hardware and software for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Mount a Canon EOS 5Ds (Model DS526521) with a Canon EF 35mm f/2 IS USM Lens (Model 9523B002) on a Diagnostic Instruments Heavy Duty Boom stand.
Attach a fixed power supply (Glorich Model #WP-AC08030V) to the camera.
Position the camera pointing down toward the table top, maintaining a distance of 29.5 cm from the lens to the tile surface (verified by stacking two tiles).
Use a small bubble T-level to ensure the table and camera are in the same plane.
Install Canon EOS Utility on a laptop and connect the camera via a USB-A to Micro-B USB 3.0 cable.

steps.title: Construct Lighting Rigs
steps.instruction: Assemble four lighting rigs to provide consistent illumination.

substeps.instruction: Assemble 4 Savage Studio Light Kits (Savage LED30 bulbs, 5500K, 35W).
Set the top of the stand to 27.5 inches above table level and attach the lamp at a 45° angle.
Zip-tie a power supply to the base of each stand.
Attach two clamp lights to each side (left and right): one with the bulb center at 18 inches above table level and one at 4 inches.
Center each rig on each 25-inch side of the diffuser box, placed as close as possible without touching and equidistant on each side.
Adjust all lights to point directly at the center of the tile stage.

steps.title: Assemble Diffuser Box
steps.instruction: Build a cuboid diffuser structure to soften light.

substeps.instruction: Construct a 25" x 25" x 36" (tall) cuboid using 25-inch PVC pipes for the squares and 36-inch PVC pipes for the vertical connectors.
Attach diffuser cloth to each face using two spring clamps on the horizontal top bar and one on each vertical bar (use a single clamp for adjacent vertical sides).
Position the box so the camera boom enters the box touching one of the vertical pipes.

steps.title: Prepare Samples for Imaging
steps.instruction: Arrange alcohol-stored 14-day pitfall samples on the imaging surface.

substeps.instruction: Mark off a 12- by 12-inch ceramic tile.
Arrange all individuals, labels, and the color selector card/reference ruler within a rectangle 8 inches wide by 12 inches long.
Place the color selector card in the bottom right and all tube labels in the bottom left of the rectangle.

steps.title: Set Up Project Directory Structure
steps.instruction: Create the following directory hierarchy to avoid path problems with FIJI scripts: PROJECT /IMAGES/ [Site Specific Directories] / 1_RAW/ (.CR2 files), /2_CROPPED/ (.TIF files), /3_BINARY/ (red binary .TIF), /4_ROI/ (.ROI files), /5_RESULTS/ (.CSV measurements), /6_CHOP/ (individual .TIF images in subdirectories), /7_TAXA/ (.CSV with taxon IDs), /8_COLOR/ (color data).

steps.title: Capture Images
steps.instruction: Configure camera settings and capture the samples.

substeps.instruction: Turn on all lights and set Savage LED60K to maximum.
In Canon EOS Utility, select 'Remote Shooting'.
Set camera parameters: F-stop = F22, Shutter Speed = 1/30, ISO = 500.
Select 'Live View Shoot'. Set Focus to FlexiZone = 'Single' and Continuous AF = 'On'.
Use the cursor to set the autofocus zone on the smallest organisms in the image.
Select the target folder and capture the image, saving it to /PROJECT/IMAGES/1_RAW/SITE/.

steps.title: Crop and Convert Images
steps.instruction: Process raw files into TIFF format using Adobe Photoshop.

substeps.instruction: Open the .CR2 photo in Photoshop and apply the previously created Camera Profile.
Rotate from horizontal to vertical if necessary.
Crop the image so only the tile is shown, ensuring all individuals, labels, and the color selector card are visible.
Save as a .tif file with: Image Compression = 'None', Pixel Order = 'Interleaved', and Byte Order = 'Macintosh' (if applicable). Layer Compression should be none.

steps.title: Create Red Binary Image
steps.instruction: Use FIJI to isolate organisms from the background.

substeps.instruction: Open the cropped .tif in FIJI. Go to Image -> Adjust -> Color Threshold.
Set Thresholding method = MaxEntropy, Threshold color = Red, and Color Space = RGB.
Initial settings: Red (0, 255), Green (0, 170), Blue (0, 120).
Increment the second blue value by 10 units if light organisms are missing, but reduce it if shadows create 'fuzz' around edges.
Save the binary file as a .tif.
Use the white eye-dropper and rectangle tool to cover unwanted features (labels, tile edges) and fill with white (Cmd-D).
Use the pencil tool (line width 2) with white color to separate touching organisms.
Use the red eye-dropper and pencil/paint brush to fill in missing parts of organisms.
Save and replace the binary file.

steps.title: Extract Morphometrics and ROI
steps.instruction: Measure organism dimensions and save regions of interest in FIJI.

substeps.instruction: Open the red binary file in FIJI.
Set Scale: Distance in Pixels = 27, Known distance = 1, Unit of length = mm.
Set Measurements: Area, Bounding Rectangle, Shape Descriptors, Centroid, Perimeter, Fit Ellipse, and Feret's Diameter.
Go to Image -> Adjust -> Color Threshold: MaxEntropy, Black, RGB, Red (255, 255), Green (0, 0), Blue (0, 0).
Run Analyze -> Analyze particles: select 'Show overlay', 'Display results', 'Clear Results', and 'Add to manager'.
Save the results .csv file to the appropriate directory.
In the ROI manager, select 'More' and save the .roi file.

steps.title: Chop Individual Images
steps.instruction: Create separate image files for every individual using a script.

substeps.instruction: Create the script 'ROIchopchop.ijm' in PROJECT/CHOPPER/ and correct the path variable.
Manually open the CROP image and ROI file in FIJI to verify the scale.
Create a separate directory for the image in ~/PROJECT/6_CHOP/SITE/.
Update the 'eventname' variable in the script (e.g., "RMNP_002.20180917.IB.01.IMG_01") and run the script to save individual .tif images.

steps.title: Extract RGB Color Values
steps.instruction: Extract color data for each individual using a script.

substeps.instruction: Reopen the CROP and ROI files in FIJI to ensure scale consistency.
Create and save the 'colorextract.ijm' script.
Open the /2_CROPPED/ version of the image.

Run the script to: make a composite, set measurements (mean, standard, min, integrated, skewness, kurtosis, stack, display, add), measure all layers via ROI manager, and save the .csv to /IMAGES/8_COLOR/[site]/.

steps.title: Database Management
steps.instruction: Import and process data using MySQL.

substeps.instruction: Create the `PON_Loader` table for morphometrics.
Create the `PON_taxa` table for taxonomic data.
Create the `PON_Occ_Data` occurrence table and move data from `PON_Loader` to `PON_Occ_Data` using an INSERT INTO statement, then TRUNCATE `PON_Loader`.
Create `color_loader` and `color_cleaner` tables; update channel IDs (1=red, 2=green, 3=blue) and extract site, number, and ROI from labels.
Create `color_rows` table and populate it by pivoting the `color_cleaner` data for red, green, and blue channels.
Combine morphology and color data into the `PONTaxMorCol` table by joining `PON_taxa`, `PON_Occ_Data`, and `color_rows`.
